Leyla, who now resides in Poland, has launched family court proceedings and has asked customers at Costa coffee shops to look out for Mani and Zayn, as they are believed to frequently visit these establishments. The family previously lived in England before moving to Poland. Leyla, now in Poland, is seeking Mani's return due to concerns for his welfare.

U.S. travel rules for dual citizens from specified nations, including Iran, have been revised under a visa waiver program, creating uncertainty and inconvenience. This was demonstrated by BBC Persian presenter Rana Rahimpour being barred from traveling due to her Iranian citizenship, while her cousins encountered similar issues upon attempting to fly. The new regulation, also impacting Iraqi, Syrian, and Sudanese dual citizens, has provoked upset, particularly from European ambassadors who fear disproportionate and unfair treatment of such individuals.

Sky is addressing capacity issues at certain telephone exchanges due to new customer additions and the launch of Sky Go Extra, resulting in slow internet speeds for some subscribers, with areas such as Doncaster, North Wales, and Bristol reportedly affected. The company has provided an online postcode checking facility for users to check if their local exchange is impacted.

A Liverpool-based gang, led by Joseph McHale, Kevin Schruyers, and Robin Vaughan, was convicted of targeting ATMs across Scotland between August and November 2013 using explosives. The gang was found guilty of blowing up ATMs, stealing approximately £133,000, and attempting burglaries. The investigation traced the stolen money to the Mersey area, and a local unwittingly aided the gang. Sentencing has been deferred until next month.

The Scottish Prison Service is set to launch technology disruping mobile phone signals at HMP Shotts and HMP Glenochil within weeks, as per new legislation, in a bid to combat the use of contraband mobile phones linked to criminal activities, such as drug supply, organized crime, and harassment, a move that follows the illegality of mobile phone possession by prisoners since 2010.

Former French President Francois Hollande particpated in a ceremony commemorating the 70th anniversary of the Allied liberation of the Natzweiler-Struthof, Bergen-Belsen, and Jasenovac Nazi camps, all of which saw the loss of thousands of lives, including those of French resistance fighters, German Jewish diarist Anne Frank, and Croatian camp inmates. The ceremonies examined historical atrocities, ongoing social tensions, and rising attacks on both Jews and Muslims in France.

Actor Johnny Depp, 52, and his wife Amber Heard, 30, have filed for divorce citing irreconcilable differences following 15 months of marriage. The separation was initiated shortly after Depp's mother's death and involves ongoing legal repercussions from an incident where Heard imported two dogs into Australia illegally, initiating a heated public dispute with Australian Deputy PM Barnaby Joyce.

The Maersk Tigris, a Marshall Islands-flagged ship initially reported to be in international shipping lanes before being confirmed to be in Iran's waters, remains anchored off Bandar Abbas following seizure by Iranian authorities, believed to be due to a court order issued by a private Iranian company over debt-related complaints. The vessel, carrying commercial goods but no military equipment, sent a distress call that was picked up by the US Navy, leading to a US Navy destroyer and reconnaissance plane being dispatched to monitor the situation, with US officials describing the actions of Iranian patrol vessels as "inappropriate."

The article summarizes that despite a 2014 serious case review of Seren Bernard's suicide in foster care in Pembrokeshire, Sarah Pollock (Seren's sister) has not been able to access the full report due to legal restrictions, despite fresh calls, as it is a matter of public interest. The report suggests that Seren had a previous suicide attempt and further attempts were a possibility, yet her mood had lifted in the days prior to her death, with no indication of suicidal thoughts. This decision leaves Sarah feeling traumatized and struggling to learn from the review due to the report's limited disclosure.

In the Super League clash, Leigh secured a commanding 18-7 win over Salford, with key contributions from Gregg McNally and Atelea Vea helping them establish an 18-0 half-time lead. Josh Drinkwater scored a drop-goal for Salford in the second half, but their lack of game management and defensive struggles proved costly in a hard-fought loss. Leigh's success places them in a strong position entering the Super 8 qualifiers, while Salford must regain their earlier-season momentum to move up from their current fourth spot.

Paul Allen, a tech tycoon, is developing Stratolaunch Systems, a giant aircraft powered by six 747 jumbo jet engines with a 385ft wingspan, to launch unmanned rockets from high altitudes instead of traditional launch pads. The initiative, partnered with Burt Rutan, aims to provide cargo transportation for commercial satellite industries and the International Space Station. Test flights are planned for 2016, following a decade of preliminary design. Elon Musk's space company will produce the booster rocket carried by Stratolaunch, while other tech entrepreneurs like Jeff Bezos and Richard Branson are involved in private space ventures.

Derbyshire trail Lancashire by 365 runs after a career-best 89 from wicketkeeper Alex Davies helped them accumulate significant runs in the second innings, however the team lost both openers on the final day of the match, leaving them to chase a challenging target.

In his final episode of "The Daily Show," Jon Stewart was joined by Bruce Springsteen and received video messages from John Kerry and John McCain. He thanked colleagues, fans, and family, and acknowledged the show's role in shaping American political discourse. Notable alumni include Steve Carell, John Oliver, and Stephen Colbert. #JonVoyage trended on Twitter as a tribute to Stewart's tenure.

Four-time League Cup winners Forest, two-time European Cup champions, are set to kick off their latest League Cup campaign against League Two side Doncaster, three days after their Championship season opener, with goalkeeper Dorus de Vries sidelined due to an injury, but not one of serious concern.

The Arches, a culturally significant nightclub in Glasgow, entered administration after a midnight closing time was imposed due to drug abuse and disorder complaints, resulting in a 50% revenue loss and threatening 130 jobs. The Scottish Government is working to find solutions to aid in the venue's future, offering support through the Pace initiative.

A senior Provisional IRA member, Ivor Bell, was arrested and charged with complicity in the 1972 disappearance, murder, and secret burial of Jean McConville, one of the "Disappeared" during the Troubles in Ireland. McConville, a mother of 10, was accused of being an informer before her body was found in 2003. The IRA later admitted to killing and burying nine of the "Disappeared," and an independent commission has been searching since 1999 for the remains of several of them, including McConville.

Wigan Warriors secured a victory despite playing with 12 men after a red card to Ben Flower, overturning a 28-14 deficit in the second half with tries from Josh Charnley, Lewis Tierney, and Anthony Gelling. This win puts them in a position to potentially secure a home semi-final in the Super League, while the League Leaders' Shield is now favored for Warrington who need only a draw to win the first piece of Super League silverware this season.

In September, the poppy arch installation, Wave, at Yorkshire Sculpture Park attracted an unprecedented 170% increase in visitors, with around 100,000 people, compared to about 37,000 in the previous year. This nationwide tour of poppies from the artwork Blood Swept Lands and Seas of Red, which commemorates 100 years since the start of World War One, is forecasting the park's largest visitor count ever, with over half a million visitors. The sculpture is reported to provide a distinctive, "calm and contemplative" experience for many visitors.

A severe flood warning on the A361 between East Lyng and Burrowbridge was lifted on 10 March, with temporary traffic lights and a continued closure on the A372. Councillor Harvey Siggs praised the clearance efforts, urging motorists to exercise caution due to water-filled rhynes along the road.

The Subaru telescope's observation reveals a new icy body, V774104, approximately 500-1000 km in size and approximately 15.5 billion km from the Sun, making it three times further away than Pluto. Scientists are tracking its orbit to determine its shape and location within the Solar System, as it may follow an unusual path like Eris, 2012 VP113, or Sedna.

Ashley Yates, the former headteacher at The Tynings Primary School in Staple Hill, admitted to recording indecent images of children and staff using a spy pen. Police have identified additional adult victims and are offering support to them. Yates is currently in custody and will next appear in court on August 9.

Great Britain's Helen Glover and Heather Stanning defended their Olympic title in the women's pairs rowing event at the Rio Games, beating New Zealand by 1.2 seconds and extending their undefeated streak to 39 races, spanning five years.

The misunderstanding was later resolved, and McClure decided to keep her name on the tram.

The inquest into the 2014 death of 14-year-old Alice Gross in the River Brent, west London, will investigate potential government and police failures related to her case, particularly why Latvian murder convict Arnis Zalkalns, the prime suspect in Alice's death, was not monitored despite his prior conviction. Alice's family is pushing for an examination of the systems for monitoring foreign offenders and cross-border information sharing to prevent similar occurrences in the future.

The Local Data Company and University of Stirling found that Scotland's average retail vacancy rate dropped from 14.5% to 13.7%, with East Kilbride having the highest rate (33%) and Inverurie the lowest (1%). The study also revealed that over 40% of empty shops have been vacant for more than three years, with Dundee leading the highest proportion of persistent vacancy. Towns such as Anstruther, Clydebank, Dumfries, Inverkeithing, Lochgelly, Peterhead, and Pitlochry showed improvement, while five towns have maintained vacancy rates at less than 6% for the last three years, including Inverurie, Ellon, North Berwick, Dunbar, and Biggar. At the other end of the scale, rates in five towns have remained above 22% over the last three years - Banff, Dumbarton, Cumbernauld, East Kilbride, and Ardrossan. The research highlighted that long-term vacant units imply obsolescence and negatively impact the success of struggling towns.

Rory McWhirter, a Scottish man from Edinburgh, was sentenced to prison for a sophisticated fraud scheme, where he deceived individuals into applying for fake jobs, obtained marriage certificates, registered fake births, and fraudulently claimed tens of thousands of pounds in benefits under false identities. His attorney argued that he would be able to repay the money if not jailed, as the funds were being used for his property business venture.

Authorities are attempting to demolish Awamiya's old quarter, a predominantly Shia area, as reported militant activity hideout, but activists claim security forces are displacing residents, leading to clashes, fatalities, and property damage. The UN has condemned the demolition, as it threatens the area's historical and cultural heritage. The region has been marked by conflicts since the 2011 Arab Spring uprisings, with escalating anti-government protests following the execution of a prominent Shia cleric, Sheikh Nimr, in 2016.

Young people in Belfast express frustration over lack of job opportunities, feel let down by politicians who focus on personal gain instead of skills-training workforce and promoting positive social changes like drug reform and better healthcare.

In Barnet, Andrew Travers resigned as chief executive following the EU referendum in June 2016, where voters were initially unable to vote due to missing names on poll lists. An independent investigation has been launched, with interim leadership by John Hooton, and the review will conclude by the end of May, presenting its findings to the General Functions Committee.

Manager Neil Warnock has given midfielder Peter Whittingham, who celebrated ten years at the club last month and whose contract expires this summer, time to consider a new deal. Whittingham, who opened the scoring in the Bluebirds 2-0 win over Preston, will be looking to add to his tally against Norwich City on Saturday, while Warnock has indicated that Wales international Emyr Huws and fellow midfielder Stuart O'Keefe are not part of his long-term plans, with Huws going on loan to Ipswich and O'Keefe joining League One side MK Dons.

Surprised about the issue at higher levels, Fleming suggested expanding funding for the Tennis Integrity Unit. He reassured that the Australian Open is free of such activities.

A 60-year-old local man, believed to be a customer, entered a bank in Northfield, produced a firearm without making threats or demands, and held a female staff member in an interview room for about an hour. Newport County AFC, co-tenants of Rodney Parade along with rugby teams Newport Gwent Dragons and Newport RFC, are facing criticism from an opposing team's manager over the condition of the pitch, particularly after multiple game disruptions. Olive Cooke, a 92-year-old resident of Bristol, has been a dedicated poppy collector for the Royal British Legion for over 75 years, with her service dating back to her youth, following her father's footsteps as an active member after World War One. For the past 12 years, she has sold poppies at the Bristol Cathedral's entrance. Her dedication stems from the loss of her first husband, Leslie Hussey-Yeo, in 1943 during World War II and a deep appreciation for the sacrifices made by young men during both world wars, many of whom were her school friends. The RBL appreciates her as their "most-valued poppy collector."

Shimon Peres, instrumental Israeli politician involved in the nation's birth in 1948, twice as prime minister, president, and a Nobel Peace Prize laureate in 1994 for peace accords, passed away after a major stroke at the age of 93.

This includes launching a children's iPlayer, forming partnerships with cultural bodies, funding local reporters to support local news, developing an "Ideas Service" for understanding the world, and prioritizing quality drama. The commission calls for accurate information and respectful debate from politicians, criticizes the government's aborted plan to demand companies disclose foreign worker proportions, and suggests a review of hate crime sentences.

She endorsed Lisa Duffy as the best candidate to lead UKIP, advocating for the party to break free of its hard-right image, undergo internal reform, and shift towards the center-ground in order to grow and thrive.

Reviews have been mixed for her portrayal of the grotesque, drunk, and vile Miss Hannigan, but the musical's unashamed optimism is seen as a rejuvenating force following recent terrorist attacks.
